title: What Happens When You Drink an Energy Drink?
description:
Send this to the coworker who calls an energy drink 'lunch'.
Energy drinks range from 54 to 328 mg of caffeine per 16 fluid ounces (FDA), about six times apart. You can feel caffeine within about 15 minutes, it's absorbed within about 45, and with a half-life of about five hours, half is still in you five hours later. Too much can mean jitters, a racing heart and lost sleep. The FDA cites 400 mg a day for most adults, and medical experts advise against energy drinks for children and teens. A preliminary 2026 AHA conference abstract (not peer-reviewed) found heart events mentioned more often in FDA adverse-event reports involving caffeine and stimulant products; it shows an association, not proof, and not your personal risk. Questions about your heart? See a doctor.
